name: Magnetically spread arc nitrogen fixation
summary: From 1907 Norsk Hydro at Notodden ran Birkeland-Eyde furnaces, where a magnet spread an electric arc into a disc that turned air into nitrogen oxides for fertilizer.
description: Electric-arc nitrogen fixation in which a magnetic field spreads the arc into a disc through which air passes, forming nitric oxides for conversion to nitrate fertilizer.
tier_reason: The scoped record is a particular configuration, local witness, trial or material application. Dependence across fields or generations on THIS referent is not established; do not inherit the importance of its broader missing family.

impact.note: First industrial fixing of nitrogen from air, but regional in supply and soon superseded with few successors; scores imply tier 2, below the reviewed tier 1.

why: Norway had abundant cheap hydroelectric power, and farming worldwide depended on limited Chilean nitrate, so electricity-hungry nitrogen fixation could pay there.

market.note: The process was used in industrial nitrate-fertilizer production; this does not establish the first transaction.

evidence.supports: Dates the experimental furnace operation and larger-scale industrial use of Birkeland–Eyde furnaces at Notodden.
Explains the spread disc-shaped arc, its calcium-nitrate product and comparison with cyanamide and other electric-arc approaches.

date.label: 6 April 1934
date.basis: The nomination dates extinguishing the last Notodden Birkeland–Eyde furnaces to 6 April 1934.

events.statement: Notodden’s last Birkeland–Eyde arc furnace was extinguished.
events.caveats: This is the endpoint at Notodden only. The nomination records Rjukan arc operation until 1940, and the technical museum identifies one Rjukan furnace retired in 1940; general chemical production at Notodden continued beyond 1934.

evidence.supports: Reports the final Birkeland–Eyde furnace at Notodden was extinguished in 1934 and distinguishes this from the 1968 chemical-plant closure.
Dates the last Notodden Birkeland–Eyde furnaces being extinguished to 6 April 1934 at 17:00.

date.basis: The technical museum dates retirement of this preserved Rjukan furnace to 1940.

events.statement: A Rjukan Birkeland–Eyde furnace now preserved by Norsk Teknisk Museum was taken out of service in 1940.

events.population: Operators of the named Rjukan furnace
events.caveats: The nomination records Rjukan furnaces to 1940 but also describes particular plants as used until 1928; the relationship of these statements is unresolved. This witness does not establish the last use of every Rjukan furnace or of the process worldwide.
